prompt: Which category has the sharpest seasonal swing, and how far ahead would you need to act on it?
title: Seasonal Swing Lead Time
summary: The prompt asks which category shows the sharpest seasonal swing and how much lead time is needed to respond. It implies comparing categories by seasonality magnitude and identifying the earliest action window required.
executed_sql_queries:
WITH monthly_category_sales AS (
  SELECT
    p.category_id,
    DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_date) AS month,
    SUM(oi.total_amount) AS monthly_sales
  FROM retail.orders o
  JOIN retail.order_items oi
    ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
  JOIN retail.products p
    ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
  GROUP BY p.category_id, DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_date)
), category_stats AS (
  SELECT
    category_id,
    MAX(monthly_sales) AS peak_month_sales,
    MIN(monthly_sales) AS trough_month_sales,
    MAX(monthly_sales) - MIN(monthly_sales) AS peak_to_trough_difference,
    MAX(monthly_sales) - MIN(monthly_sales) AS seasonal_swing_magnitude
  FROM monthly_category_sales
  GROUP BY category_id
)
SELECT *
FROM category_stats
ORDER BY category_id;

WITH monthly_category_sales AS (
    SELECT
        p.category_id,
        DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_date)::date AS month,
        SUM(oi.total_amount) AS monthly_sales
    FROM retail.orders o
    JOIN retail.order_items oi
        ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    JOIN retail.products p
        ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
    GROUP BY p.category_id, DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_date)::date
), ranked AS (
    SELECT
        category_id,
        month,
        monthly_sales,
        monthly_sales - LAG(monthly_sales) OVER (PARTITION BY category_id ORDER BY month) AS month_to_month_change,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY category_id ORDER BY monthly_sales DESC, month ASC) AS rn_desc,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY category_id ORDER BY monthly_sales ASC, month ASC) AS rn_asc
    FROM monthly_category_sales
)
SELECT
    category_id,
    MAX(CASE WHEN rn_desc = 1 THEN month END) AS peak_month,
    MAX(CASE WHEN rn_desc = 1 THEN monthly_sales END) AS peak_month_sales,
    MAX(CASE WHEN rn_asc = 1 THEN month END) AS trough_month,
    MAX(CASE WHEN rn_asc = 1 THEN monthly_sales END) AS trough_month_sales,
    MAX(CASE WHEN rn_desc = 1 THEN monthly_sales END) - MAX(CASE WHEN rn_asc = 1 THEN monthly_sales END) AS peak_to_trough_difference,
    MAX(month_to_month_change) AS max_month_to_month_increase,
    MIN(month_to_month_change) AS max_month_to_month_decrease
FROM ranked
GROUP BY category_id
ORDER BY category_id;

WITH monthly_category_sales AS (
    SELECT
        p.category_id,
        DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_date)::date AS month,
        SUM(oi.total_amount) AS monthly_sales
    FROM retail.orders o
    JOIN retail.order_items oi
      ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    JOIN retail.products p
      ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
    GROUP BY p.category_id, DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_date)::date
), category_stats AS (
    SELECT
        category_id,
        MAX(monthly_sales) AS peak_month_sales,
        MIN(monthly_sales) AS trough_month_sales,
        MAX(monthly_sales) - MIN(monthly_sales) AS peak_to_trough_difference
    FROM monthly_category_sales
    GROUP BY category_id
), top_category AS (
    SELECT category_id
    FROM category_stats
    ORDER BY peak_to_trough_difference DESC
    LIMIT 1
)
SELECT
    m.category_id,
    m.month,
    m.monthly_sales,
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM m.month) AS month_num
FROM monthly_category_sales m
JOIN top_category t
  ON m.category_id = t.category_id
ORDER BY m.month;
